tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: How does the woman describe her previous company's culture?

options.A: Weird.
options.B: Efficient.
options.C: Tolerant.
options.D: Toxic.

questions.cn: 女士如何描述她上一家公司的文化？

optionsCn.A: 古怪。
optionsCn.B: 高效。
optionsCn.C: 宽容。
optionsCn.D: 有毒。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his company's managers?

options.A: They are arrogant.
options.B: They are ignorant.
options.C: They are ambitious.
options.D: They are accommodating.

questions.cn: 关于他公司的管理者，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们很傲慢。
optionsCn.B: 他们很无知。
optionsCn.C: 他们很有野心。
optionsCn.D: 他们很随和。

questions.stem: What does the woman say the employees in her new company can do?

options.A: They can think big.
options.B: They can air their views.
options.C: They can break conventions.
options.D: They can work flexible hours.

questions.cn: 女士说她新公司的员工能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们可以志存高远。
optionsCn.B: 他们可以发表自己的看法。
optionsCn.C: 他们可以打破惯例。
optionsCn.D: 他们可以弹性工作。

questions.stem: What does the man say about constructive feedback?

options.A: It can alter people's mindsets.
options.B: It can lead to new discoveries.
options.C: It enables people to learn and grow.
options.D: It is conducive to critical thinking.

questions.cn: 关于建设性的反馈，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它能改变人们的心态。
optionsCn.B: 它能带来新发现。
optionsCn.C: 它使人能够学习和成长。
optionsCn.D: 它有助于批判性思维。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: How are you enjoying your new job?
lines.cn: M：你的新工作干得怎么样？

lines.t: F: So far, so good.
lines.cn: F：到目前为止还不错。

lines.t: F: I don't miss having managers who deliver blunt, harsh feedback in the name of efficiency.
lines.cn: F：我不怀念那种以效率为名、给出直白刺耳反馈的管理者。

lines.t: M: From the way you described your last company, no wonder they had a problem with high staff turnover.
lines.cn: M：从你对上一家公司的描述看，难怪他们的员工流失率很高。

lines.t: F: Yeah, I couldn't wait to get out of there once my contract expired.
lines.cn: F：是啊，合同一到期我就迫不及待想离开那里。

lines.t: F: The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.
lines.cn: F：把直率置于一切之上的公司文化，问题在于它会营造出一种由“才华横溢的混蛋”构成的有毒文化，把人赶走，并从内部自我侵蚀。

lines.t: M: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings.
lines.cn: M：我们公司的管理者往往很随和友善，为了不伤感情而忽视错误和问题。

lines.t: M: Issues often get ignored there until they build up and reach a crisis point.
lines.cn: M：那里问题常常被忽略，直到积累起来、到达危机的临界点。

lines.t: F: That's not surprising.
lines.cn: F：这不奇怪。

lines.t: F: My new company seems to employ a feedback policy that combines compassion and directness.
lines.cn: F：我的新公司似乎采用了一种把体恤与直率结合起来的反馈政策。

lines.t: F: Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree, and discuss problems in real time.
lines.cn: F：员工有权发声、给出反馈、表达不同意见，并实时讨论问题。

lines.t: F: It seems to help us to course correct, improve, and meet challenges, while also building teams that collaborate and care for one another.
lines.cn: F：这似乎有助于我们及时纠偏、改进、迎接挑战，同时也建立起相互协作、彼此关心的团队。

lines.t: M: But that would be based on an atmosphere of mutual trust, wouldn't it?
lines.cn: M：但那得建立在相互信任的氛围之上，对吧？

lines.t: M: Otherwise people might interpret feedback as some kind of personal attack.
lines.cn: M：否则人们可能把反馈理解为某种人身攻击。

lines.t: F: True.
lines.cn: F：没错。

lines.t: F: Without an atmosphere of trust, feedback can create stress and self-doubt.
lines.cn: F：没有信任的氛围，反馈会带来压力和自我怀疑。

lines.t: F: But I think when we get feedback from someone we trust, we understand that the feedback isn't some kind of personal attack.
lines.cn: F：但我觉得，当我们从自己信任的人那里得到反馈时，我们会明白那不是人身攻击。

lines.t: F: It's actually a kind of support, because it's offered in the spirit of helping us improve.
lines.cn: F：它实际上是一种支持，因为它是出于帮助我们改进的心意而给出的。

lines.t: F: I think sometimes people need to shift their mindsets around how they receive feedback.
lines.cn: F：我觉得有时人们需要转变自己接收反馈的心态。

lines.t: M: Yes.
lines.cn: M：是的。

lines.t: M: Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow.
lines.cn: M：毕竟，建设性的反馈正是我们学习和成长的方式。

lines.t: M: It's the basis for healthy parenting, lasting friendships, career development, and so much more.
lines.cn: M：它是健康的养育、持久的友谊、职业发展等等的基础。

lines.t: M: If we shelter our children, friends, and colleagues from information that might enrich and enhance their lives, we're not being caring.
lines.cn: M：如果我们把那些可能丰富和改善孩子、朋友、同事生活的信息挡在他们之外，我们并不是在关心他们。

lines.t: M: We're actually doing harm to them.
lines.cn: M：我们其实是在伤害他们。

lines.t: F: That's exactly right.
lines.cn: F：完全正确。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the man say about his holiday?

options.A: He kept looking for the best place to stay.
options.B: He met many tourists from other countries.
options.C: He had a great time sightseeing and relaxing.
options.D: He managed to visit a different city each day.

questions.cn: 关于他的假期，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他一直在找最佳住处。
optionsCn.B: 他遇到了许多来自其他国家的游客。
optionsCn.C: 他观光、放松，过得很愉快。
optionsCn.D: 他设法每天游览一座不同的城市。

questions.stem: What does the woman say people tend to do when making decisions?

options.A: Prioritize what is essential to their best advantage.
options.B: Stretch out the process in search of the optimal.
options.C: Deliberate the consequences that may occur.
options.D: Take all relevant factors into consideration.

questions.cn: 女士说人们做决定时往往怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 优先考虑最有利于自己的事。
optionsCn.B: 为追求最优而拉长过程。
optionsCn.C: 仔细琢磨可能发生的后果。
optionsCn.D: 把所有相关因素都考虑在内。

questions.stem: What has made decision-making increasingly difficult?

options.A: Time pressure.
options.B: Tight budget.
options.C: Modern technology.
options.D: Fierce competition.

questions.cn: 是什么让做决定变得越来越难？

optionsCn.A: 时间压力。
optionsCn.B: 预算紧张。
optionsCn.C: 现代技术。
optionsCn.D: 激烈竞争。

questions.stem: According to the woman, what should people do when making important decisions? From the four choices, mark A, B, C, and D.

options.A: Research as many different options as possible.
options.B: Avoid going over the same options repeatedly.
options.C: Focus on what is practical.
options.D: Trust their gut instinct.

questions.cn: 根据女士，人们做重要决定时应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 尽可能多地研究不同选项。
optionsCn.B: 避免反复琢磨同样的选项。
optionsCn.C: 专注于实际可行的事。
optionsCn.D: 相信自己的直觉。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: How was your holiday?
lines.cn: F：你假期过得怎么样？

lines.t: F: Not too many other tourists around, were there?
lines.cn: F：周围游客不多吧？

lines.t: M: No, very few relatively.
lines.cn: M：不多，相对而言很少。

lines.t: M: But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place.
lines.cn: M：但我发现自己不停从一个住处换到另一个住处，想找到最完美的地方。

lines.t: M: It made me realize that indecision is a big, problem for me.
lines.cn: M：这让我意识到优柔寡断是我的一个大问题。

lines.t: M: Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.
lines.cn: M：我没有在放松，而是在寻找最佳地点。

lines.t: F: It seems you suffer from fear of better options.
lines.cn: F：看来你患上了“害怕有更好选择”症。

lines.t: F: I've read about it.
lines.cn: F：我读到过这方面的内容。

lines.t: F: It describes this loop of indecision as part of our programming.
lines.cn: F：它把这种犹豫不决的循环描述为我们心理程式的一部分。

lines.t: F: Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hardwired to optimize.
lines.cn: F：本质上，我们总倾向于把决策过程拉长，因为作为人类，我们天生就要追求最优。

lines.t: F: We have always looked to get the best things we can, as a sort of survival of the fittest.
lines.cn: F：我们一直在设法获得所能得到的最好的东西，作为一种适者生存。

lines.t: F: Optimizing isn't the problem, but rather the process that we go through.
lines.cn: F：追求最优并不是问题，问题在于我们所经历的那个过程。

lines.t: M: Well, that makes me feel better.
lines.cn: M：嗯，这让我感觉好一些。

lines.t: F: But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization.
lines.cn: F：但我认为多亏了技术，我们更容易做比较，也更容易获得选择与个性化定制的机会。

lines.t: F: We can now see what we could have, how we might get it, and what others have that we might want.
lines.cn: F：我们现在能看到自己可以得到什么、如何得到，以及别人拥有什么而我们也可能想要的。

lines.t: F: We keep looking over and returning to the same options again and again.
lines.cn: F：我们反复回看、一遍又一遍地回到同样的选项上。

lines.t: M: Yes, fear of better options offers little benefit.
lines.cn: M：是的，害怕有更好选择几乎没什么好处。

lines.t: F: It's an ailment of abundance.
lines.cn: F：这是富足带来的病症。

lines.t: F: You must have choices to have that fear of missing out on better options.
lines.cn: F：你必须有很多选择，才会产生那种“怕错过更好选项”的恐惧。

lines.t: M: Yes, I need to note when I'm worrying about inconsequential things, I guess.
lines.cn: M：是的，我想我需要留意自己什么时候在为无关紧要的事操心。

lines.t: M: If I'm spending too much time worrying over what to have for lunch, I'm robbing myself of the energy to focus on the things that matter.
lines.cn: M：如果我花太多时间纠结午饭吃什么，我就剥夺了自己专注于重要事情所需的精力。

lines.t: F: Exactly.
lines.cn: F：正是。

lines.t: F: But for more important matters, I think gut instinct might be overrated.
lines.cn: F：但对于更重要的事，我觉得凭直觉也许被高估了。

lines.t: F: When you have 30-odd options, trusting your gut is not practical.
lines.cn: F：当你有三十来个选项时，相信直觉并不实际。

lines.t: F: What you need to do is research, have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can.
lines.cn: F：你需要做的是调研、有一套流程、投入时间去探索选项，并尽可能多地排除掉一些。

lines.t: F: The most toxic part of decision-making is going over the same options time and time again.
lines.cn: F：决策中最有害的部分，就是一遍又一遍地反复琢磨同样的选项。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did the 2006 research find about homework?

options.A: It is beneficial to poor as well as rich communities.
options.B: It is conducive to children's future development.
options.C: It is welcome to parents but not to children.
options.D: It is not of much help to younger children.

questions.cn: 2006 年的研究关于作业发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它对贫困社区和富裕社区都有益。
optionsCn.B: 它有利于孩子未来的发展。
optionsCn.C: 它受家长欢迎但不受孩子欢迎。
optionsCn.D: 它对年幼的孩子帮助不大。

questions.stem: What do experts think of homework requiring internet access?

options.A: It may put some students in remote areas at a disadvantage.
options.B: It gives the majority of students ready access to their teachers.
options.C: It effectively improves the learning quality of students in rural areas.
options.D: It can bridge the learning gap between kids of different backgrounds.

questions.cn: 专家如何看待需要上网的作业？

optionsCn.A: 它可能使一些偏远地区的学生处于不利地位。
optionsCn.B: 它让大多数学生能随时联系到老师。
optionsCn.C: 它有效提高了农村地区学生的学习质量。
optionsCn.D: 它能弥合不同背景孩子之间的学习差距。

questions.stem: What conclusion could be drawn from the study in Germany?

options.A: Diligent students tend to do their homework independently.
options.B: The focus of homework should always be on school subjects.
options.C: Doing homework exerts a positive effect on kids' personality development.
options.D: The benefits of doing homework vary widely from individual to individual.

questions.cn: 从德国的这项研究中可以得出什么结论？

optionsCn.A: 勤奋的学生往往独立完成作业。
optionsCn.B: 作业的重点应始终放在学校科目上。
optionsCn.C: 做作业对孩子的个性发展有积极作用。
optionsCn.D: 做作业的益处因人而异，差别很大。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: The role of homework in classrooms is not a new debate.
lines.cn: 家庭作业在课堂中的角色并不是一个新话题。

lines.t: Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters of homework.
lines.cn: 许多家长和老师都是家庭作业的热烈支持者。

lines.t: But do all students benefit from homework?
lines.cn: 但所有学生都能从作业中受益吗？

lines.t: A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students, but not so much for younger kids.
lines.cn: 2006 年的一篇研究论文提出，对初高中生而言，学生完成作业的量与未来学业成就之间存在某种相关性，但对更小的孩子则没有那么多关联。

lines.t: A Stanford study in 2014 suggested that the same was true for students in California's affluent communities.
lines.cn: 斯坦福大学 2014 年的一项研究显示，对加利福尼亚州富裕社区的学生来说也是如此。

lines.t: The findings challenged the idea that homework was inherently good.
lines.cn: 这些发现挑战了“作业本身就有益”这一观念。

lines.t: The researchers concluded that there was an upper limit to the correlation between homework and achievement, suggesting that high school students shouldn't be doing more than two hours of homework a night.
lines.cn: 研究者得出结论：作业与成绩之间的相关性存在上限，这意味着高中生每晚做作业不应超过两小时。

lines.t: And the most valuable kind of homework for elementary level children was simply assigned free reading.
lines.cn: 而对小学阶段的孩子来说，最有价值的作业就是简单地布置自由阅读。

lines.t: The topic gets more complicated when we talk about the divide between rural and urban communities.
lines.cn: 当谈到农村与城市社区之间的差距时，这个话题就变得更复杂了。

lines.t: Studies found that in remote areas, the poor quality or lack of internet access can put students at a disadvantage because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires internet access.
lines.cn: 研究发现，在偏远地区，网络质量差或没有网络会使学生处于不利地位，因为这些地区 70% 的教师布置的作业需要上网。

lines.t: But one in three households doesn't have internet.
lines.cn: 但三分之一的家庭没有网络。

lines.t: Experts assert homework requiring the internet isn't fair.
lines.cn: 专家断言，要求上网的作业并不公平。

lines.t: While the debate continues about the effect of homework on academic achievements, there are studies focusing on other benefits of homework.
lines.cn: 关于作业对学业成绩影响的争论仍在继续，同时也有研究关注作业的其他益处。

lines.t: A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.
lines.cn: 德国的一项研究发现，作业可能对学生的人格产生影响，表明做作业也许有助于孩子变得更有责任心、更独立地学习。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about Goddard's idea of using rockets for space exploration?

options.A: It was something he apologized for later.
options.B: It was ridiculed by the New York Times.
options.C: It was a forty-nine-year plan.
options.D: It was considered visionary.

questions.cn: 关于戈达德把火箭用于太空探索的想法，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 这是他后来为之道歉的想法。
optionsCn.B: 它被《纽约时报》嘲讽。
optionsCn.C: 它是一项为期 49 年的计划。
optionsCn.D: 它被认为很有远见。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Goddard's first rocket launch?

options.A: It was of great significance to rocket science.
options.B: It was completed in the state of New Mexico.
options.C: It was somehow delayed about 12 minutes.
options.D: It failed due to a sudden change of weather.

questions.cn: 关于戈达德的首次火箭发射，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它对火箭科学意义重大。
optionsCn.B: 它是在新墨西哥州完成的。
optionsCn.C: 它不知何故延迟了约 12 分钟。
optionsCn.D: 它因天气突变而失败。

questions.stem: Why did Goddard move to New Mexico?

options.A: A laboratory and test range was already set up there.
options.B: Its climate was ideal for year-round rocket launching.
options.C: A weather expert invited him to go there for his mission.
options.D: Its remote valleys were appealing to him and his family.

questions.cn: 戈达德为什么搬到新墨西哥州？

optionsCn.A: 那里已经建好了实验室和试验场。
optionsCn.B: 那里的气候适合全年发射火箭。
optionsCn.C: 一位气象专家邀请他去那里执行任务。
optionsCn.D: 那里偏远的山谷吸引了他和家人。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Goddard's achievements?

options.A: He won an award from the US government for his work.
options.B: He gained recognition from rocket scientists worldwide.
options.C: He was granted over 200 patents in rocket technology.
options.D: He boosted the military strength of the United States.

questions.cn: 关于戈达德的成就，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他因自己的工作获得了美国政府的奖项。
optionsCn.B: 他获得了全世界火箭科学家的认可。
optionsCn.C: 他在火箭技术方面获得 200 多项专利。
optionsCn.D: 他提升了美国的军事实力。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Robert Goddard, an American born in 1882, is widely regarded as the world's first rocket scientist.
lines.cn: 罗伯特·戈达德，一位生于 1882 年的美国人，被广泛认为是世界上第一位火箭科学家。

lines.t: At age 27, Goddard published his first book, in which he hypothesized that a rocket launched from Earth could reach the moon.
lines.cn: 27 岁时，戈达德出版了他的第一本书，在书中他提出假说：从地球发射的火箭可以到达月球。

lines.t: Like many visionaries, the young scientist encountered numerous skeptics.
lines.cn: 和许多有远见的人一样，这位年轻科学家遭遇了无数怀疑者。

lines.t: In January 1920, the New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration.
lines.cn: 1920 年 1 月，《纽约时报》嘲讽了戈达德关于火箭可用于太空探索的理论。

lines.t: 49 years later, Apollo 11 reached the moon, and the famed newspaper published an apology to Goddard.
lines.cn: 49 年后，阿波罗 11 号登上了月球，这家著名报纸向戈达德公开道歉。

lines.t: Goddard launched his first rocket from an aunt's farm in his native Massachusetts in March 1926.
lines.cn: 1926 年 3 月，戈达德在他家乡马萨诸塞州一位姑妈的农场上发射了他的第一枚火箭。

lines.t: His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere three seconds.
lines.cn: 他的首次火箭之旅只持续了三秒钟。

lines.t: It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters.
lines.cn: 飞行高度仅有 12 米。

lines.t: Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.
lines.cn: 尽管如此，这仍是火箭科学的一个里程碑。

lines.t: Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches.
lines.cn: 戈达德后来咨询了一位气象专家，确定新墨西哥州全年都适合发射火箭。

lines.t: In 1930, Goddard and his family relocated there, to a remote valley in the southwest of the country.
lines.cn: 1930 年，戈达德和家人迁往那里，定居在该州西南部一处偏远的山谷。

lines.t: There, he established a laboratory and test range.
lines.cn: 在那里，他建起了一座实验室和试验场。

lines.t: However, the ambitious scientist received negligible support from the government.
lines.cn: 然而，这位雄心勃勃的科学家从政府得到的支持微乎其微。

lines.t: For four years, wealthy businessman Daniel Guggenheim provided Goddard with an annual $25,000 grant to pursue his dreams.
lines.cn: 在四年里，富商丹尼尔·古根海姆每年为戈达德提供 25,000 美元的资助，支持他追逐梦想。

lines.t: Other rocket enthusiasts also raised funds for him.
lines.cn: 其他火箭爱好者也为他筹集资金。

lines.t: Over time, Goddard's rockets grew more sophisticated and included the installation of instruments.
lines.cn: 随着时间推移，戈达德的火箭变得越来越精密，还加装了仪器。

lines.t: In spite of his many successes, Goddard was never able to interest the U.
lines.cn: 尽管取得了许多成功，戈达德始终未能引起美国

lines.t: S.
lines.cn: 军

lines.t: military in rocket-propelled weapons.
lines.cn: 方对火箭推进武器的兴趣。

lines.t: He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.
lines.cn: 他获得了 200 多项专利，并一直开拓火箭技术，直到 1945 年去世。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about working for a new venture?

options.A: It requires entrepreneurial experience.
options.B: It is usually financially rewarding.
options.C: It can be quite frustrating.
options.D: It can be rather risky.

questions.cn: 关于为新创企业工作，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它需要创业经验。
optionsCn.B: 它通常在经济上回报丰厚。
optionsCn.C: 它可能相当令人沮丧。
optionsCn.D: 它可能相当有风险。

questions.stem: What has science demonstrated regarding the positive culture of a new venture?

options.A: It contributes to rapid business expansion.
options.B: It inspires willingness to make sacrifices.
options.C: It reduces conflict among team members.
options.D: It encourages creation and innovation.

questions.cn: 关于新创企业积极的文化，科学已经证明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它有助于业务的快速扩张。
optionsCn.B: 它激发做出牺牲的意愿。
optionsCn.C: 它减少团队成员之间的冲突。
optionsCn.D: 它鼓励创造与创新。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about entrepreneurs at the initial stage of a new venture?

options.A: They have unrealistic expectations.
options.B: They often work without any pay.
options.C: Few can find willing investors.
options.D: Many are idealistic dreamers.

questions.cn: 关于新创企业初创阶段的创业者，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们抱有不切实际的期望。
optionsCn.B: 他们常常完全没有报酬地工作。
optionsCn.C: 很少有人能找到愿意投资的投资者。
optionsCn.D: 许多人是理想主义的梦想家。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Working for a new venture comes with a lot of risks.
lines.cn: 为一家新创企业工作伴随着很多风险。

lines.t: There's instability, unclear responsibilities, and the need to be a master of all trades.
lines.cn: 有不稳定性、职责不清，以及必须样样精通的要求。

lines.t: But the primary benefit is usually the passion and excitement associated with playing a role in a promising new company.
lines.cn: 但主要的好处通常是热情与兴奋——因为在一家前景光明的新公司里扮演了一个角色。

lines.t: The person to thank for that passion and excitement is almost always the entrepreneur.
lines.cn: 要为这种热情和兴奋道谢的人，几乎总是那位创业者。

lines.t: There's something about the founder's energy and enthusiasm that infects the rest of the team.
lines.cn: 创始人的精力和热忱，有一种能感染整个团队其他成员的力量。

lines.t: The willingness to take risks may inspire others to be more courageous.
lines.cn: 勇于冒险可能激励他人更有勇气。

lines.t: The optimism and positivity may motivate people to focus less on trivial and unimportant matters.
lines.cn: 乐观与积极可能促使人们少关注琐碎和不重要的事情。

lines.t: The celebration of milestones may prompt staff to be more grateful about their own accomplishments and privileges.
lines.cn: 庆祝里程碑可能促使员工更感激自己的成就和所拥有的条件。

lines.t: What becomes set in the firm's culture is a contagious collection of affirmative and positive emotions, which are usually shared among the team.
lines.cn: 最终固化进公司文化的，是一组具有传染性的积极肯定情绪，通常在团队中共享。

lines.t: Science has already done a good job of proving the results that follow.
lines.cn: 科学已经很好地证明了随之而来的结果。

lines.t: These include better processes, greater team cohesion, reduced conflict, and sharper alertness.
lines.cn: 这些结果包括更好的流程、更强的团队凝聚力、更少的冲突和更敏锐的警觉。

lines.t: But what is yet to be demonstrated is whether the founder's passion leads to increased team performance.
lines.cn: 但尚未被证明的是：创始人的热情是否带来团队绩效的提升。

lines.t: This was recently tested in research, which analyzed the teams of 73 new companies across a range of industries, such as IT, medicine, and energy.
lines.cn: 这一点最近在一项研究中得到检验，该研究分析了 IT、医疗、能源等多个行业 73 家新公司的团队。

lines.t: The CEOs were consulted once again years after the initial analysis, and most shared their firm's performance reports so that their success could be more objectively measured.
lines.cn: 在初次分析数年之后，研究者再次咨询了这些 CEO，大多数人分享了公司的业绩报告，以便更客观地衡量其成功。

lines.t: Entrepreneurial teams generally progress through three phases.
lines.cn: 创业团队通常经历三个阶段。

lines.t: The first is inventing a product or service.
lines.cn: 第一阶段是发明一种产品或服务。

lines.t: The second is founding the venture to sell that product or service.
lines.cn: 第二阶段是创办企业来销售该产品或服务。

lines.t: And the third is developing the firm so it continues to grow.
lines.cn: 第三阶段是发展公司，使其持续增长。

lines.t: The researchers discovered that when the team is passionate about the third phase, developing the firm, there's a clear link to performance.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，当团队对第三阶段——发展公司——充满热情时，与绩效有明显的关联。

lines.t: But the first phase, a passion for invention, is not a reliable indicator that the firm will still be open for business a few years later.
lines.cn: 但第一阶段，即对发明的热情，并不能可靠预示这家公司几年后仍在营业。

lines.t: Likewise, the second, the passion for founding the venture doesn't necessarily translate into greater success.
lines.cn: 同样，第二阶段，即对创办企业的热情，也不必然转化为更大的成功。

lines.t: The solution to great team performance stems from a willingness to recruit others who could direct their passion towards the third phase of entrepreneurialism, developing the business.
lines.cn: 出色团队绩效的解法在于：愿意招揽那些能把热情投向创业第三阶段——发展业务——的人。

lines.t: Employing more staff can in itself be a risk for an entrepreneur, as is paying them big dollars to attract them.
lines.cn: 对创业者来说，多雇人本身可能就是一种风险，付高薪来吸引人才也是如此。

lines.t: On many occasions, the entrepreneurs reported not paying themselves a wage at all initially in order to cover salaries and expenses.
lines.cn: 在许多情况下，创业者报告说自己起初根本不给自已发工资，以便支付员工薪水和各项开支。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the possible reason why women tend to live longer?

options.C: They are born with a stronger ability to socialize.
options.D: They are better able to survive or handle disease.

questions.cn: 关于女性为什么往往更长寿的可能原因，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 她们有更好的饮食习惯。
optionsCn.B: 她们承担的社会责任更少。
optionsCn.C: 她们天生社交能力更强。

questions.stem: What is the recent discovery about human cells?

options.B: They depend on adequate sleep to thrive.

options.D: They strengthen with regular exercise.

questions.cn: 关于人类细胞，最近的发现是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们的繁殖能力是有限的。
optionsCn.B: 它们依赖充足的睡眠来生长。

questions.stem: What do many public health policymakers believe?

options.B: Improved health care for the elderly will contribute to longevity.

options.D: The resolution of age-related diseases will solve the mystery of ageing.

questions.cn: 许多公共卫生政策制定者相信什么？

optionsCn.A: 衰老过程最终可以被控制。
optionsCn.B: 改善老年人医疗保健有助于长寿。
optionsCn.C: 预防心脏病和中风会提高预期寿命。
optionsCn.D: 解决与年龄相关的疾病将解开衰老之谜。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Aging is a curious thing, and people's desire to beat it, and death, has become an industry worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
lines.cn: 衰老是件奇妙的事，而人们战胜衰老和死亡的渴望，已经成为一个价值数千亿美元的产业。

lines.t: Despite the huge investment into research, aging remains somewhat obscure, although there are certain things researchers do understand.
lines.cn: 尽管研究投入巨大，衰老仍在某种程度上晦暗不明，不过研究者确实理解一些事情。

lines.t: They know that women tend to have longer lifespans, living on average six years longer than men.
lines.cn: 他们知道女性往往寿命更长，平均比男性多活六年。

lines.t: No one is really certain of the reason for this, although the speculation centers around the idea that women are more capable of surviving or handling disease than men.
lines.cn: 没有人真正确定其中原因，不过推测集中在这一点上：女性比男性更能存活下来或应对疾病。

lines.t: For virtually every disease, the effects are greater on men than they are on women.
lines.cn: 几乎每一种疾病，对男性的影响都大于对女性的影响。

lines.t: Some suggest that women's immune systems benefit from their tendency to prioritize and nurture social connections, but for me, this explanation is hardly convincing.
lines.cn: 有人提出，女性免疫系统的优势得益于她们重视并经营社会关系的倾向，但对我来说，这个解释很难让人信服。

lines.t: Researchers also know, to an extent, what causes aging.
lines.cn: 研究者在一定程度上也知道是什么导致了衰老。

lines.t: For 60 years, it was believed that cells would continue to divide forever.
lines.cn: 60 年来，人们一直认为细胞会永远分裂下去。

lines.t: It was only uncovered in relatively recent times that older people's cells divide a smaller number of times than younger people's.
lines.cn: 直到相对晚近，人们才发现老年人的细胞分裂次数少于年轻人的细胞。

lines.t: Only cancer cells, in fact, are capable of dividing forever.
lines.cn: 事实上，只有癌细胞才能无限分裂。

lines.t: Human cells have a limited reproductive ability.
lines.cn: 人类细胞的繁殖能力是有限的。

lines.t: To an extent, we can postpone the eventual stop of cells dividing through nutrition, exercise, good sleep, and even relaxation techniques.
lines.cn: 在某种程度上，我们可以通过营养、锻炼、良好睡眠甚至放松技巧，来推迟细胞分裂最终停止的时刻。

lines.t: But we cannot stop the aging process, and researchers are yet to answer the ultimate question of aging.
lines.cn: 但我们无法阻止衰老过程，研究者也仍未回答关于衰老的终极问题。

lines.t: Why does the body ultimately fall to pieces?
lines.cn: 身体最终为什么会崩解？

lines.t: In the opinion of some of the world's best scientific minds on the subject, part of the reason we don't yet have an answer is because many researchers are looking in the wrong direction.
lines.cn: 在这个问题上，世界上一些最杰出的科学头脑认为，我们至今没有答案的部分原因是，许多研究者找错了方向。

lines.t: Many public health policymakers believe that the resolution of age-associated disease will tell us something fundamental about the aging process.
lines.cn: 许多公共卫生政策制定者相信，解决与年龄相关的疾病，会让我们从根本上了解衰老过程。

lines.t: But, say some top scientists, that's completely erroneous.
lines.cn: 但一些顶尖科学家说，这完全错了。

lines.t: They point to when the diseases of childhood were eliminated, but this did not provide any insight into childhood development.
lines.cn: 他们指出，儿童疾病被消灭时，并没有让我们对儿童发育有任何洞见。

lines.t: In the same way, the idea that the resolution of age-associated disease like heart disease and stroke will inform us about aging is not based on sound science or logic.
lines.cn: 同样，“解决心脏病、中风等与年龄相关的疾病就能让我们了解衰老”这一想法，并不基于严谨的科学或逻辑。

lines.t: At best, if the major causes of death in developed countries were eliminated, this would only add a decade to average life expectancy.
lines.cn: 充其量，如果把发达国家的主要死因都消除，也只能让平均预期寿命增加十年。

lines.t: But while there is money available to be spent on it, the search to understand the secrets of aging will be ongoing.
lines.cn: 但只要还有钱可花在这上面，探索衰老奥秘的努力就会继续下去。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Good afternoon.
lines.cn: 下午好。

lines.t: In today's talk, we'll discuss how managers can get their staff to do what they are asked.
lines.cn: 在今天的讲座里，我们要谈管理者如何让员工按要求行事。

lines.t: Much to their frustration, managers often struggle to get their staff to comply with even simple instructions.
lines.cn: 令管理者十分沮丧的是，他们常常连让员工遵守简单的指令都很困难。

lines.t: Often they blame their employees.
lines.cn: 他们往往责怪自己的员工。

lines.t: They don't read emails.
lines.cn: 他们不看邮件。

lines.t: They don't listen.
lines.cn: 他们不听。

lines.t: They don't care.
lines.cn: 他们不在乎。

lines.t: That kind of thing.
lines.cn: 诸如此类。

lines.t: But according to recent research conducted in Australia, it looks like it's not the employees' fault, but the managers'.
lines.cn: 但根据最近在澳大利亚进行的一项研究，看来这不是员工的错，而是管理者的错。

lines.t: It's easy to understand why people sometimes disobey procedures intentionally.
lines.cn: 人们有时故意不遵守规程，原因不难理解。

lines.t: Occasionally, it's because they're pressured to finish in a short time.
lines.cn: 有时是因为他们被压在短时间内完成。

lines.t: At other times, they may disagree with the spirit of the procedure, the effort demanded, the time consumed, the lack of potential effectiveness.
lines.cn: 另一些时候，他们可能不认同规程的初衷、所要求的投入、所消耗的时间，以及潜在效果的不足。

lines.t: And every now and then, they just don't want to, maybe deliberately or out of stubbornness.
lines.cn: 还有时候，他们就是不想做，也许是故意的，也许是出于固执。

lines.t: So apart from that, what else gets in the way of procedural compliance?
lines.cn: 那么除此之外，还有什么会妨碍人们对规程的遵守？

lines.t: The research scholars surveyed 152 blue-collar workers from two separate sites in the mining industry.
lines.cn: 研究学者调查了采矿业两个不同场地的 152 名蓝领工人。

lines.t: They asked the workers a range of procedure-related questions, such as whether they found the procedures useful, how confident they felt in their job, how comfortable they were to speak up in the workplace, and how closely they followed any new procedures set by their managers.
lines.cn: 他们向工人询问了一系列与规程相关的问题，比如规程是否有用、他们对工作有多自信、在职场中发声有多自在，以及他们多大程度上遵守管理者制定的新规程。

lines.t: They were also asked to rate the extent to which they perceived their supervisors to be helpful.
lines.cn: 他们还被要求评价自己感知到的上级的帮助程度。

lines.t: That last statement was the most instructive because, as the researchers found, there was a remarkably strong correlation between how helpful supervisors were perceived to be and how likely their employees were to follow their directives.
lines.cn: 最后一项最有启发性，因为研究者发现，上级被认为有多乐于帮助，与员工有多可能遵从他们的指示之间，存在极其强的相关性。

lines.t: Supervisors helping behavior was found to be motivational in nature.
lines.cn: 上级的帮助行为被发现具有激励作用。

lines.t: It increased employees' perception of the likelihood of success in the attainment of job goals and therefore fostered a willingness to dedicate their effort and ability to their work.
lines.cn: 它提高了员工对达成工作目标可能性的感知，从而培养了他们把精力和能力投入工作的意愿。

lines.t: In short, managers should be ongoing role models for the change.
lines.cn: 简言之，管理者应当是这场变革中持续的榜样。

lines.t: As the saying goes, do as I do, not as I say.
lines.cn: 正如俗话所说：照我做的做，而不是照我说的做。

lines.t: To affect behavioral change, what's most required is interaction and involvement, the human touch, and naturally, processes that add value.
lines.cn: 要促成行为改变，最需要的是互动与参与、人情味，当然还有能带来价值的流程。

lines.t: Although procedures are designed to guide and support employees' work, employees, it seems, can't always be expected to comply with procedures that are not seen as useful.
lines.cn: 尽管规程的设计初衷是引导和支持员工的工作，但看起来，不能总指望员工去遵守那些被认为没用的规程。

lines.t: And, of course, managers shouldn't keep resending emails.
lines.cn: 当然，管理者也不该反复重发邮件。

lines.t: They're an effective tool for the sharing of data and reports, but they're a hopeless tool if what a manager is desiring is a change in behavior.
lines.cn: 邮件是共享数据和报告的有效工具，但如果管理者想要的是行为的改变，它就是个没用的工具。
